correctness.rationale: Removing the weak edge gives a spanning-tree coordinate torus, and the even length of its cycle path makes the removed edge aligned at z=0. The potential is E=−Σα_e cos z_e+w cos(cᵀz), with exact update z⁺=z−hK∇E. The rank-one Hessian D−wccᵀ loses its first positive direction at w=1/A and has kernel v there. In the weighted chord inequality, nonzero equality requires every successive increment on the unit circle to be the same nonzero vector times 1/a_j. Three distinct collinear unit points are impossible, so equality still forces all path deviations to vanish; the pendant terms force the same on other edges. For w>w_c there is a negative direction. Eliminating stationary transverse directions analytically leaves an even energy with quadratic coefficient A(1−wA)/2 to first order in w−w_c and quartic (A³−B₃)/24>0 at w_c. The divided derivative has one small positive root in s² above threshold, yielding two local minima and square-root displacement; compactness and critical uniqueness put every nearby-parameter global minimum on those branches. In centered vertex coordinates the critical Hessian is positive semidefinite and dominated by the usual positive Laplacian; thus the displayed step gives positive strict contraction multipliers off the one neutral mode. The left projection ℓ kills the linear gradient and satisfies ℓᵀK=vᵀ/Q. The center graph has no quadratic term because the map has no quadratic term and I−L_stable is invertible. Projecting the cubic along z=tv+O(t³) gives t⁺=t−h(A³−B₃)t³/(6Q)+O(t⁵). Local strong-stable tracking transfers the center-orbit asymptotic to the actual projected coordinate with exponentially small error: the leaf over zero contracts exponentially; all other center orbits have eventual sign and the telescoped inverse square grows at twice the cubic coefficient. Finally Q is the squared norm of the zero-mean vertex profile p solving Bᵀp=v; adding a leaf duplicates p_r before recentering and increases Q by N p_r²/(N+1). For the unit path Q is the variance sum of m+1 consecutive integers, m(m+1)(m+2)/12. For example the four-edge unit path has Q=10; a leaf at its endpoint increases Q to 40/3 and lowers the rate from 2h to 3h/2 at a common admissible h. originality.rationale: The supported distinct contribution is the weighted odd-unicyclic critical discrete-time law, notably the explicit coefficient based on the full centered vertex profile and its attachment law, together with the weighted symmetry-breaking analysis. value.rationale: The useful distinction is between where frustration destabilizes the minimizing spin pattern and how rapidly the critical map actually relaxes. Arbitrarily weighted pendant trees are invisible to the effective-resistance threshold yet can change the exact observable rate even for identical cycle weights. The explicit variance/attachment rule and codimension-one exception make this a usable comparison across graphs, not a repeated Laplacian threshold computation.
